extraction_notes: Transfer and output curves were digitized at a minimal point set for an F2 attempt; values are approximate reads from the plotted traces.
The transfer curve uses the TA = 25 degC trace from Fig. 2. Its x axis is linear and y axis is logarithmic; VDS = 10 V and pulsed are stated in the figure.
Three representative output curves from Fig. 1 were retained at VGS = 3 V, 5 V, and 10 V. The figure does not state temperature or pulse conditions.

No capacitance-versus-VDS figure is published. Ciss, Coss, and Crss are available only as table values at VDS = 25 V, VGS = 0 V, f = 1 MHz; a VDMOS capacitance fit must use a constant gate-drain capacitance assumption and cannot model Crss collapse.

The RDS(ON) table publishes typical and maximum values: typical 1.2 ohm (maximum 2 ohm) at VGS = 10 V, ID = 0.5 A, and typical 1.4 ohm (maximum 3 ohm) at VGS = 5 V, ID = 0.05 A. The schema records the typical values for curve fitting.
The datasheet does not publish body-diode reverse-recovery time trr or reverse-recovery charge Qrr.
The datasheet also includes RDS(ON)-versus-temperature, reverse-diode, SOA, power-dissipation, and transient-thermal-resistance figures, but they were omitted from this minimum extraction set.
extraction.omission_reason: F2 curve extraction is usable for transfer and output behavior, but no capacitance-versus-VDS curve or body-diode reverse-recovery data is published. Capacitance collapse and reverse recovery therefore cannot be independently fitted; the available capacitance table supports only an approximate constant-capacitance transient model.
